ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, point $C$ is a point on $\odot O$, the bisector of $\angle CAB$ intersects $\overset{\frown}{BC}$ at point $D$, a line is drawn through point $D$ such that $DE\parallel BC$ and it intersects the extension of $AC$ at point $E$. $DE$ is a tangent line of $\odot O$; if $DE=2$ and $CE=1$, find the length of $BD$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Connect CD,\\
$\because$ $\angle OAD = \angle CAD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\overset{\frown}{CD} = \overset{\frown}{BD}$,\\
$\therefore$ CD = BC,\\
In $\triangle CED$, $\angle E = 90^\circ$, DE = 2, CE = 1,\\
$\therefore$ $CD = \sqrt{DE^2 + CE^2} = \sqrt{2^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ BD = $\boxed{\sqrt{5}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A is on the left side, B is on the right side, O is located near the middle of AB, and AB is in the position of a horizontal diameter; C is at the upper left of the circle, D is at the upper right of the circle, and E is located higher up and near the extension direction of AC. Corresponding to the meaning of the problem in the figure: D is on arc BC, DE is drawn through D, and DE is parallel to BC and intersects the extension line of AC at E. Reasoning: Because A, O, B are collinear, and AD is the angle bisector of ∠CAB, ∠CAD = ∠DAB, that is, ∠CAD = ∠OAD. Two equal inscribed angles correspond to equal arcs, so arc CD = arc DB, and the corresponding chords are equal, so CD = BD. Also because AB is the diameter of circle O, and C is on the circle, ∠ACB = 90°, that is, AC ⟂ BC. Since DE ∥ BC, and E is on the extension line of AC, CE ⟂ DE, and triangle CED is a right triangle. It is known that CE = 1, DE = 2, so CD = √(CE² + DE²) = √(1² + 2²) = √5. Also CD = BD, therefore BD = √5.
